artists.biography: Carter the Unstoppable Sex Machine (frequently shortened to Carter USM) are an English indie rock band formed in 1988 by singer Jim "Jim Bob" Morrison and guitarist Les "Fruitbat" Carter. They made their name with a distinctive style of power pop, fusing samples, sequenced basses and drum machines with rock 'n' roll guitars and off-beat wordplay-loaded lyrics. They reached the height of their fame in 1992. Over the following years the band took on new members, topping out as a six-piece, but struggled to regain their earlier popularity. They initially split up in 1998 after releasing seven albums.

They made their name with a distinctive style of power pop, fusing samples, sequenced basses and drum machines with rock 'n' roll guitars and off-beat wordplay-loaded lyrics. They reached the height of their fame in 1992. Over the following years the band took on new members, topping out as a six-piece, but struggled to regain their earlier popularity. They initially split up in 1998 after releasing seven albums.

perplexity.description:
Straw Donkey... The Singles is a 1995 compilation album by Carter the Unstoppable Sex Machine, released on Chrysalis Records, collecting the band's key singles from their early career spanning 1988 to 1997. Formed in 1987 by Fruitbat (guitarist Les Carter) and Jim Bob (vocalist Jim Morrison), the duo pioneered a raw, innovative sound blending punk-pop with electronic elements like drum machines, samples, and distorted guitars, all laced with sharp social commentary on British life, politics, and urban decay. Tracks like "Sheriff Fatman," "The Only Living Boy in New Cross" (a UK Top 20 hit), "After the Watershed (Early Learning the Hard Way)," "Rubbish," and "Lean on Me (I Won't Fall Over)" exemplify their satirical edge and anthemic energy, drawing from rock's aggression and electronic's mechanical pulse to critique Thatcher-era Britain.

The original album features 15 standout singles, including non-album cuts like "A Sheltered Life," "Anytime Anyplace Anywhere," "Bloodsport for All," and the 11-minute closer "Born on the 5th of November," which was issued as a single from the compilation. It serves as an essential primer to the band's irreverent style, earning positive nods for its high-energy hits and cult appeal, though specific review scores remain sparse. Later reissues, such as the 2023 expanded Straw Donkey... The Complete Singles edition, enhance this legacy with newly remastered audio by Phil Kinrade, additional promo tracks ("Road Rage," "Stuff the Jubilee!," etc.), a restored DVD of videos with band commentary, and a booklet of song stories, cementing its status as a definitive retrospective.
